key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs and proves a conditional error analysis for the indirect approach.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a principled way to train PINNs for PDE-constrained control problems while tracking how approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft constraint errors affect reliability.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control, trained on a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control, trained on the first-order optimality system.
Error framework: decomposes total error and derives a conditional residual-to-error bound with a computable indicator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems, including a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear equation with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint.
watch_item: The reliability guarantee is conditional on regularity, network approximability, soft-constraint residual control, and staying near the reference optimal solution, so performance may weaken outside that regime.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
